title: Choosing three from ten

prereqs.why: This is the definition of a binomial coefficient, applied once.
Deciding whether order matters is deciding what an outcome is.

statement:
A committee of **three** people is to be chosen from **ten**. The committee has no roles: the three members are interchangeable.

How many different committees are possible?
hints: First settle whether order matters. Would choosing Ada, then Grace, then Alan give a different committee from choosing Alan, then Ada, then Grace?
Count the ordered choices first: $10 \times 9 \times 8$. Then ask how many times each committee was counted in that total.
Each committee of three was counted once for each of the $3! = 6$ orders in which its members could be picked. Divide.

payload.label: Committees
payload.syntax: A whole number. You can write C(10,3) or 10!/(3!*7!) and it will be worked out.
